extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('host') is passed directly into os.system() via string concatenation. An attacker controlling the 'host' parameter can execute arbitrary shell commands on the server.

User-controlled data (request.body or request.GET.get('blob')) is deserialized via pickle.loads(). An attacker can send a crafted pickle payload to achieve arbitrary code execution (RCE) on the server.

User input from request.GET.get('fragment') is passed directly into jinja2.Template() and rendered. Jinja2 templates can be abused with {{7*7}} or {{constructor}} to execute code or inject HTML/script content into the rendered response.

User input from request.GET.get('ref') is used directly in a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../') in the 'ref' parameter to write files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, including overwriting system files via ss/card injection.

User input from request.GET.get('name') is used directly in file path construction without traversal protection. Combined with request.body, an attacker can overwrite arbitrary files within or outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR using path traversal sequences.

Server-Side Request Forgery via urllib.urlopen with unvalidated SSL: cert verification is disabled (ssl._create_unverified_context()). The endpoint URL is hardcoded but could be extended. SSRF also present via request.URL patterns.

User input is hashed using MD5 (hashlib.md5) which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks. This endpoint allows any user-provided phrase to be hashed, providing no security value.

SSL certificate verification is disabled (ssl._create_unverified_context()). An attacker on the network path could perform a man-in-the-middle attack and serve arbitrary data from the partner endpoint.

User input from request.GET.get('lane') is passed directly to Django's redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL with an external domain (e.g., ?lane=https://evil.com) to create an open redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User-controlled Origin header is reflected into Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. While this is CORS misconfiguration, it enables cross-origin requests if the origin pattern is attacker-controlled, potentially allowing CSRF-adjacent attacks.

cwe: CWE-942: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Security headers are disabled: X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is set to empty string, removing browser-side XSS protection.
SSN and credit card numbers are written to disk in plaintext: request.GET.get('ssn', '111-22-3333') and request.GET.get('card', '4111111111111111'). Sensitive PII is stored unsafely.

cwe: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: DEBUG=True is the default fallback when SECRET_KEY falls back to 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-me'. In production, this default value would be used as the SECRET_KEY, making sessions easily forgeable.

DEBUG defaults to True when DEBUG env var is not explicitly False. Debug mode exposes detailed error pages with source code, template context, stack traces, and database information to end users — a production environment must have DEBUG=False.

Hardcoded database credentials 'crmuser:crmpass@localhost:5432' in dj_database_url default. These credentials are visible in source code and may leak into version control, logs, or container environment dumps.
Admin user password 'adminpass123' is hardcoded in seed_data management command. Default credentials are easily identifiable in source code.
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is set based on 'not DEBUG' — meaning in DEBUG mode (which defaults to True), session cookies are sent over HTTP. This exposes session tokens to network sniffing.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Session' Cookie Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Sensitive internal information (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env value and BASE_EXPORT_DIR path) is exposed via JSON response to any authenticated user. Internal settings reveal deployment details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Raw request body and authorization header are logged via logger.warning(), potentially exposing sensitive credentials or tokens in log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
